properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **OPTION (c) — INIT ASKS.** Alex's literal request, taken over the recommendation recorded on this node, which was (b) *"apply the instruction-pointer policy to MCP configs"*. He chose with (b)'s argument and (c)'s stated costs both in front of him.

⭐ THE STRONGEST CASE FOR HIS CHOICE, which the pre-decision text under-weighted: **(b) GUESSES, AND A WRONG GUESS IS SILENT.** Detection reads a fresh repo that has no signal, falls back to the primary harness, and hands an OpenCode user a `.mcp.json` their tool never opens — with nothing to tell them anything is missing. Asking is the only option on the list that cannot be silently wrong, and a silent wrong install is the exact failure class this project keeps finding (`cap:degraded-surface`'s diagnosis not reaching a by-name caller; the loop nudge registered against a script that is not there; the pointer written into a file the harness never reads). **A question costs one prompt; a silent miss costs a user who concludes reflow2 does not work.**

⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED LATER: the one-liner install becomes a conversation, which is in tension with `user-iterative-release-preference` (*one-liner install, one word to update*). So the non-interactive path is not optional garnish — it is part of the requirement: a flag must carry the answer, and a non-tty must never hang. CI, scripted installs and `adopt` runs are the common path, not the exception.

📌 WHAT (c) DOES NOT SETTLE: the instruction-pointer policy stays as it is (already narrow and correct), and the loop-nudge asymmetry is a separate open question (`dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`) where the problem runs the other way — too little, not too much. Option (d), labelling the generated files, was not chosen but composes with (c) and remains available.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══

RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` for a project should be more like a CLI wizard that asks you what agent harness you are utilizing (Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, open code, etc.) and only installs the necessary file changes based on your choice. It needs the correct mcp setup, the graph artifact that can be git committed and the agents.md reference."*

✅ HIS THREE NAMED ESSENTIALS ARE ALL ALREADY PRODUCED on HEAD (`cbb1a19`): the MCP setup, the committed export at `docs/design/<project>.json` (since PR #172), and the `AGENTS.md` reference. **Nothing he needs is missing — the complaint is that things nobody asked for arrive alongside them.**

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE QUESTION: `tools/reflow2_init.py` ALREADY IMPLEMENTS ALEX'S PRINCIPLE — for instruction files — AND THE OPPOSITE ONE FOR MCP CONFIGS, ABOUT 150 LINES APART. Both deliberate, each carrying its reasoning in a comment, and they contradict each other.

  · INSTRUCTION POINTERS (`pointer_targets`, `CREATE_IF_NO_INSTRUCTION_FILE`) — appends only to instruction files the project ALREADY OWNS; when it owns none, creates just `CLAUDE.md`. The comment rejects the alternative in as many words: *"writing GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and the rest into a repo that asked for none of them is **spam**, and the sidecar we create (AGENTS.md) already IS the agents.md convention that the others increasingly follow."*
  · MCP CONFIGS (`MCP_CONFIGS`) — writes `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` AND `.vscode/mcp.json` unconditionally: *"One generator, several files — a project opened in a different tool should just work."*

⇒ So the question was never "should init ask?" but "which of init's two existing policies is right?" — and (c) settles it toward the narrow one, by asking rather than by inferring.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) LEAVE IT — extras are inert. Counter: init's own code calls that spam one screen away, and a first-time user read it as clutter.
(b) APPLY THE POINTER POLICY TO MCP CONFIGS — detect, falling back to the primary harness. No prompt, internally consistent. **Counter that decided it: detection has no signal on a fresh repo, which is exactly when init runs, so it guesses — and guesses silently.**
(c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — ASK, with `--harness=…` for non-interactive use.
(d) INSTALL ALL, BUT LABEL each file with which tool reads it and that deleting it is safe. Not chosen; composes with (c).
(e) ASK ONLY WHEN AMBIGUOUS — detect, prompt when detection is empty. Not chosen; two code paths, and behaviour that differs between a fresh and an established repo.

📌 SCOPE, because it makes the change smaller than it sounds: most of what `init` writes is HARNESS-NEUTRAL and untouched — `AGENTS.md`/`REFLOW2.md`, the committed export, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`. The harness-specific surface is the three MCP configs, the instruction pointer (already policy-correct), and the loop-nudge hook.

⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD; an older `init` may have written a different set of files than what he saw.
properties.name: DECIDED — `init` ASKS which harness you use and installs only that one's files (option c), settling init's two contradictory install policies in favour of the narrow one
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. Two things are deliberately on the record rather than smoothed away: that the choice went AGAINST the option this node recommended, and the reason his choice is nonetheless the stronger one — detection guesses, and a wrong guess about which harness will open a repo produces a silent failure, which is the failure class this project has now hit four separate times. The pre-decision text is kept in full beneath the outcome because `req:roads-not-taken` makes the rejected options part of the record, and because the instruction-pointer contradiction it documents is a real finding about `reflow2_init.py` that survives whichever option was taken.
